brewing.notes: A safe starting point for yellow tea: treat it like a delicate green tea.

description:
A shrubby, medium-leaved tea plant native to the Dongting hills around Yueyang in Hunan. It is seed-propagated, diploid and mid-season.

Used as raw material for green and yellow teas of good quality.
history: It is the main variety grown in its home area and suits Hunan's green tea districts. The plant has a half-spreading habit, dense branching and bright green oval leaves with a raised surface. Spring growth starts in late March and peaks at the one-bud-three-leaf stage in mid April, with yields near 150 kg per 667 square metres, and it stands up well to cold and drought.
processing: A plant cultivar, not a processing style: it is usually made into yellow tea, and the method is up to the grower.
harvest_season: Spring buds appear in late March; the one-bud-three-leaf flush peaks in mid April.
appearance_dry: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_liquor: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_wet: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
taste_profile: Depends on how the leaf is processed; tea from it usually falls within what yellow teas give.
vintage_note: Spring one-bud-two-leaf samples, dried, hold about 3.8% amino acids, 24.1% tea polyphenols, 12.7% catechins and 4.2% caffeine.
